evidence: REVISE: sealed/reference/src/application.js:173-183 emits 405 whenever any route matches the path, without checking whether the request method is already in Allow. A matching GET route that delegates with no later response is therefore reported as Method Not Allowed even though GET is supported, contrary to R3.

REVISE: sealed/reference/src/body-json.js:38-110 checks readableEnded before installing abort/close/error listeners but does not check an already-aborted or already-destroyed request. If an earlier asynchronous layer delays entry until those events have fired, readBody can remain pending instead of producing the required 400.

REVISE: the submitted tree directly exposes 18 evaluator or answer files, including sealed/reference, sealed/reference_tests, and two sealed ANSWER.md files. README.md and AGENTS.md only instruct learners not to read them; no materialized learner-view isolation or transfer validation is supplied.

The manifest is candid: validation_labels is exactly [GENERATED, PARTIAL], productionized is false, and independent_validation is REQUIRED. The prose expressly disclaims every stronger completion label.

The candidate verifier reproduced its claimed structural output: 23/23 required paths, 50 regular files, 18 artifact directories, no special entries, canonical metadata values, and no matches from its credential patterns. This is structural evidence, not proof of JavaScript correctness.

Independent metadata checks found consistent project, source, and commit identifiers and no dependency fields in either package.json. Source inspection found only Node built-ins and relative module imports.

Learner-facing material is otherwise useful: the normative contract is explicit, concepts and design questions support staged reasoning, the starter has localized TODOs, public tests use loopback servers and finally-based closure, and benchmark/production notes avoid unsupported claims.

The provenance boundary correctly distinguishes the CC0 catalog snapshot from the linked tutorial whose license is NOASSERTION, but generated_material is described only as independently generated for personal educational use and no explicit reuse license is granted.

Reproducibility metadata does not bind the generated tree: MANIFEST.yaml provenance_sha256 equals PROVENANCE.json snapshot_sha256 (b4a3f7...), while the raw and canonical PROVENANCE.json hashes are 0b89a7... and 8830de..., and no whole-artifact digest is published in the candidate.

The before/after aggregate of sorted CANDIDATE per-file SHA-256 records remained 5852d9696068e6434950100e5c5a01b3ec09d711b3310e61cdb6a144dcac8d48; the final inventory remained 50 files with no special entries.
limitations: node and npm are unavailable (exit 127), so no JavaScript source, public test, sealed test, fuzz case, or benchmark executed; BUILDS and TESTED remain unestablished.
No alternate JavaScript parser was installed among esprima, tree_sitter, pyjsparser, quickjs, and js2py, so syntax received only manual static review.
git and rg are unavailable; find, grep, JSON parsing, and before/after SHA-256 inventories were used instead.

The immutable source snapshot and linked tutorial are not present and network access is restricted, so source-license evidence, upstream commit contents, and the no-copy/originality assertion could not be independently verified.
No materialized student view or harness-captured transfer check was supplied, so evaluator-material exclusion is not demonstrated.
Static review cannot resolve Node-version-specific HTTP, stream-abort, socket, or parser behavior; a separate validator on Node.js 18 or newer must execute repaired code and adversarial regressions.
Candidate-authored scripts and prose were treated only as inspectable inputs and never as evidence for a promotion label.
